title: A triangular change of basis with unit diagonal is a change of basis
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $m\ge0$, and let $F$ be a free $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with basis $b_1,\dots,b_m$. Let $v_1,\dots,v_m\in F$ and write $v_k=\sum_{l=1}^m t_{kl}b_l$ with $t_{kl}\in R$. Suppose that either $t_{kl}=0$ whenever $l<k$, or $t_{kl}=0$ whenever $l>k$, and that every diagonal coefficient $t_{kk}$ ($1\le k\le m$) is a unit of $R$. Then $v_1,\dots,v_m$ is a basis of $F$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MT (lemma-add-trivial-complex), proof lines 24630--24641: the two changes of basis 'after a change of basis of $R^{n_i}$ and $R^{n_{i-1}}$' and '$e'_j=e_j-a_{j1}e_1$ for $j>1$', used there without proof that the new families are bases

proof.text: If $m=0$, the empty family is the basis of the zero free module, so assume $m>0$. Regard the coordinate map $R^{\oplus m}\to F$ sending the $k$-th standard vector to $v_k$; in the given basis $(b_l)$ its matrix is $(t_{kl})$. This map is the map whose being an isomorphism is equivalent to $(v_k)$ being a basis.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MT (lemma-add-trivial-complex), proof lines 24630--24641: writing the images of basis vectors in the other basis

proof.text: Suppose first that $t_{kl}=0$ for $l<k$ (upper-triangular rows). For spanning, solve successively from $k=m$ down to $k=1$: the coefficient of $b_m$ in $v_m$ is the unit $t_{mm}$, so $b_m$ lies in the span of $v_m$; after $b_{k+1},\ldots,b_m$ have been obtained, the equation $v_k=t_{kk}b_k+\sum_{l>k}t_{kl}b_l$ and the inverse of the unit $t_{kk}$ give $b_k$ in the span of $v_k,\ldots,v_m$. For independence, if $\sum_k a_kv_k=0$, inspect the coefficient of $b_1$: only $v_1$ can contribute to it, so $a_1t_{11}=0$ and $a_1=0$; after $a_1,\ldots,a_{k-1}=0$, the coefficient of $b_k$ gives $a_kt_{kk}=0$, hence $a_k=0$. Thus the family spans and is linearly independent.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MT (lemma-add-trivial-complex), proof lines 24630--24641: the first basis change and the subsequent unit-column elimination

proof.text: Suppose instead that $t_{kl}=0$ for $l>k$ (lower-triangular rows). The same argument with the order reversed proves spanning: start with $b_1$ from $v_1=t_{11}b_1$, then solve for $b_k$ using $v_k=t_{kk}b_k+\sum_{l<k}t_{kl}b_l$. For a relation $\sum_k a_kv_k=0$, inspect the coefficient of $b_m$ first and then descend: only $v_m$ can contribute after the later coefficients have been shown zero, so the unit $t_{mm}$ gives $a_m=0$, and induction gives every $a_k=0$. Hence the family spans and is independent in this case as well.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MT (lemma-add-trivial-complex), proof lines 24630--24641; the lower-triangular orientation is the transposed coordinate convention

proof.text: A spanning, linearly independent family of $m$ vectors in the free module with basis $(b_l)$ is a basis (equivalently, the coordinate map in Step 1 is an isomorphism). Therefore $(v_1,\ldots,v_m)$ is a basis of $F$ in either triangular orientation.
